run_order: 1. node scripts/figma/resolve-selectors.mjs docs/design-jobs/AUDIT-VERIFY/fixplans/c8-assembled.json --apply   — ONE Figma call; fills `id` on the 8 selector rows (2 hero fills + 6 zoom chips) and clears their unresolved-id flag. Ambiguous/nomatch rows are LEFT unresolved on purpose.

2. mv docs/design-jobs/AUDIT-VERIFY/fixplans/c8-assembled.resolved.json docs/design-jobs/AUDIT-VERIFY/fixplans/c8-assembled.json   — TRAP: resolve-selectors writes a SECOND file (<plan>.resolved.json) next to the first, and normalize-plans globs the whole directory. rows.expect: frame named 'Hero — SELECTED' on 52:2 — the parent of 52:160 'Wood-fired pizza, five minutes from home' and 52:161 'Open Tuesday to Sunday, from 5pm' (b08a pn column); it is the node the Inspector is describing
rows.why: F02 — Inspector BACKGROUND · Fill on 52:2 reads 52:131 '#1A56DB' (fresh read b08a) while the selected hero renders light gray. The hex is MEASURED; the hero's paint is not (a text dump carries no paint), so the repair that uses only known values is to make the canvas obey the inspector, not the reverse. Same element on both counts: the footer says the selection is 680 x 250 and the selection label 52:163 sits at board-relative x=404 y=236, so the outlined box runs roughly x 504..1184 y 111299..111549 — which contains 52:160 (642..1038) and 52:161 (730..950) and excludes the site nav row above it. No id for the frame is in any dump, so this row resolves by exact layer name: run `node scripts/figma/resolve-selectors.mjs <this file> --apply` BEFORE normalize-plans.mjs — normalize has no selector branch for op:fill (normalize-plans.mjs:115) and an id-less fill row degrades to advisory. The op is idempotent: if the frame already holds #1A56DB the applier reports SAME and writes nothing.
rows.holdWhy: F02 HELD by the parent, pending ONE read of the hero frame's fills[0].color on 52:2 and 199:205. Two reasons. (1) #1A56DB is BUILDRIK'S OWN accent (DESIGN.md's single accent colour), and this hero belongs to the mock customer site 'Bella Cucina' — painting a customer's hero in the product's brand blue is a category error, which makes the INSPECTOR SAMPLE the more likely wrong half, not the canvas. (2) op:fill has no expect guard (apply-queue enforces expect only for text and rename), so painting over an unread colour cannot be undone — the old value would never have been recorded. The read costs one call and settles which half is wrong.

rows.expect: I2143:20597;2142:11053 'section' at board-relative x=92 (row indent 92) and I2143:20605;2142:11080 'heading-that-is-long' at board-relative x=156 (row indent 156) — the two candidate rows, both parented to a frame named 'row'
rows.detail: F01 DECISION — move the LAYERS highlight to the 'section' row (I2143:20597;2142:11053); do NOT rename the other surfaces. Arithmetic for the decision: on 52:2 three text surfaces plus the outline already agree — inspector header, canvas selection label and footer all say Section/Hero, and the outlined canvas frame is literally NAMED 'Hero — SELECTED'. Moving one highlight is 1 edit; renaming every surface to the heading is 4 edits AND still leaves the outline contradicting all four, because no op in scripts/figma/apply-queue.mjs can move a selection outline. 1 beats 4-that-do-not-converge. HELD because the repair is out of the applier's reach, not because the decision is unclear: (a) the highlight is paint or a variant on the ROW INSTANCE frame and the fresh dumps carry only instance-sublayer TEXT ids, no frame ids and no paint; (b) all nine row frames are named 'row', so resolve-selectors.mjs returns AMBIGUOUS(9) by design and refuses to guess; (c) if the row is a component with a 'selected' variant, NOTHING in this toolchain can set it — normalize-plans.mjs:152-154 maps any op starting with 'setProperties' to advisory. What the applier CAN do on these instances is text: the nine rows already carry per-instance overrides of the same inner component text nodes (2142:11053 reads 'section' on one instance and 'footer' on another), so text overrides demonstrably work here. It is the highlight, not the copy, that is unreachable. THE READ THAT SETTLES IT (1 call, both boards together): for 52:2 and 199:205, list the nine row instances under the LAYERS panel returning each row's node id, fills[0].color and componentProperties. That answers which row is highlighted and whether it is a paint (then this becomes an op:fill row on I2143:20597;2142:11053) or a variant (then it is hand work in Figma).
rows.why: F01 — 52:2: highlight on 'heading-that-is-long', every other surface on the section. See VERDICTS F01.

rows.expect: TEXT 'Section · Hero', 11/Regular, box=[6356, 101491, 74, 16], parent 'Footer' on 638:2378 (S7 · Settings · General)
rows.why: F15 — a full-page Settings shell has no canvas, so it must not print a canvas selection readout or a zoom level. op:delete is HIDE (visible=false, apply-queue.mjs 'Hide, never remove'), so this is reversible. Containment arithmetic: 638:2378 is [6340,100615,1440,900]; its bottom edge is 101515. This text runs y 101491..101507 and x 6356 = board x + 16, i.e. inside the bottom 32px footer band — the SAME band 52:2 uses (Footer 52:10 at y 111915..111947, texts at 111923). That identity is the mechanism: these boards were drawn from the assembled-shell template and the footer was never made conditional. No height changes, so BRIEF rule 4 (auto-layout compensation) does not apply; if the Footer is a horizontal auto-layout its three children are hidden together and the band simply empties.

normalize-plans.mjs dry-run AFTER injecting resolved ids: read 34 -> queued 34 (24 delete, 6 fill, 4 advisory), 0 unresolved, 0 needs-review.

apply-queue.mjs OPS set does not contain 'advisory', so the 4 held rows are reported as not-executable-here and cannot run. This matters: `hold: true` is NOT read by normalize-plans.mjs or apply-queue.mjs (grep returns only prose). A held row written with a LIVE op would be normalized into a live row and applied. That is why every held row here carries op:advisory and records its real op under intended_op.

apply-queue.mjs checks `expect` ONLY for op:text and op:rename. delete/fill/resize/move have no expect guard at all — they act on whatever sits at the id. Every expect below is therefore documentation of the node's state at the 18:29 fresh read, plus the proof that the id is the node meant, not a guard the applier will enforce.
